subject: Streaming session billing: pro-rata/retry accounting and proposed pilot credit
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@novamed.com>

Cc: Novamed Finance <billing@novamed.com>

Subject: Question about streaming session billing — partial responses & retries

Hi Lauren,

We're reviewing usage from our pilot and seeing a handful of edge cases where it looks like we were charged for partial generations after client disconnects and then again after automatic retries. Our billing team has asked for a clear explanation of how Redwood counts tokens for streaming responses in three cases:

1) Network disconnect mid-generation (client receives 0 or partial tokens, reconnects and the model resumes).
2) Client retries the request due to timeout and the server emits overlapping tokens (duplicate output).
3) Transient server-side hiccup where the stream is re-sent (same trace id) — does Redwood dedupe automatically?

We attached a short session log (novamed_session_logs.txt) with two sample session_ids and timestamps that show the duplicate-looking output. Can you confirm:
- What exactly appears on the invoice line item for these sessions?
- Is there an existing grace/pro-rata window where you don't bill repeated tokens?
- If not, can we get an exception/credit for duplicates during our pilot?

We need this in the next 48 hours for our renewal discussion. Thanks,

—Samir
Samir Patel
Director of Platform Integrations
Novamed

Subject: Re: Question about streaming session billing — partial responses & retries

Hi Samir — thanks for the log and the clear examples. High level first, then a couple options we can propose for your pilot/contract: 

Short answer (how current hosted API is metered):
- We bill at the token level for tokens the runtime has emitted to the connection. In practical terms that means the invoice shows per-token consumption tied to the model/route.
- If a connection drops mid-generation, tokens already emitted are billed; tokens that were only in flight but not emitted are not billed.
- Retries are deduplicated when they present the same idempotency/request_id; otherwise retries that result in duplicate emitted tokens will be billed.

Gaps you hit and options:
- Disconnects + resume: we do not currently implement a time-based "commit" beyond emission. If the client reconnects and resumes the same logical session (and provides the same request_id), our runtime will attempt dedupe; if resume results in new emission we bill those tokens.
- Network vs server retries: server-side retransmits using the same trace/request id are deduped. Client retries that re-send without preserving idempotency are hard to dedupe.

Two options we can take for the pilot (pick 1 or both):
A) Short-term operational: we can apply a one-time pilot credit covering confirmed duplicate charges up to $4,000 while your team instruments idempotency tokens and session resume headers. We'll need your filtered invoice lines (we can help identify duplicates).
B) Contractual addendum: add a streaming-session clause — "pro-rata session billing" — where sessions under 2,000 tokens are billed with a 300-token minimum and a 3-second commit window for immediate reconnects/retransmits when the same request_id is present. This would be part of an enterprise amendment to ND-4521.

I've attached a short proposal (redwood_streaming_billing_proposal.pdf) with suggested language and instrumentation steps. If you want, we can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the sample logs and mark lines for credit. 

TL;DR: we can credit confirmed duplicate charges for the pilot up to a capped amount + propose a small-rate-card addendum with a short commit window.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications before we schedule the call: 

1) In your Option B you mention a 3-second commit window. Is that applied to any reconnect that happens within 3 seconds of the disconnect (regardless of whether the client sends the same request_id)? Or is same request_id required for the window to apply?

2) If we accept the pilot credit, what is the expected timeline for the instrumentation work on our side to avoid duplicates going forward? Our engineering team is already stretched — what's the minimal thing we must do to benefit from the dedupe logic?

Attached filtered logs that show two sessions where a retry appears to have produced 180 duplicated tokens across two reconnects. If you can mark the exact lines you believe are duplicates and the estimated charge, that would help.

—Samir

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Novamed streaming billing — recommended approach

Lauren / Marissa — quick internal note to propose a way forward: 

- Approve a pilot credit of up to $4,000 (finance to own PoV). We should require Novamed to provide the filtered invoice lines we used to verify duplicates so Finance can reconcile.
- Update the enterprise rate card language: "Streaming sessions are billed at per-token rates. For enterprise customers, Redwood may elect to apply a 3-second commit window for reconnects that supply the same request_id; client retries that do not preserve idempotency may be subject to billing. Where duplicate charges are confirmed during a pilot, Redwood will issue a one-time credit not to exceed the pilot cap."
- Offer a minimal instrumentation checklist to Novamed to make it easy: 
  1) Add idempotency request_id header on initial request; preserve it for reconnects.
  2) Use our recommended session-resume header (x-rw-session-id) when reconnecting.
  3) Include the finalization call (POST /v1/sessions/{id}/commit) for long-running streams where possible.

This buys time for the product team to consider a longer-term billing mechanic (e.g., session-level min-billing or token commit semantics) while we protect the customer and keep the contract moving. Finance will need the filtered lines and an approval note to apply the credit.

Attachment: billing_playbook_excerpt.pdf

-karthik

Subject: Re: Question about streaming session billing — pro-rata/retry accounting and proposed pilot credit

Samir — following up with a concrete proposal based on the logs you sent and internal sign-off: 

1) Pilot credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit up to $4,000 to cover confirmed duplicate charges from the pilot period. To proceed we need the invoice lines you want reviewed and the filtered log excerpts (you already sent the excerpts — thank you). Finance will reconcile and post the credit within 10 business days of confirmation.

2) Short-term rate language: We'll add an amendment to ND-4521 with the following operative language (summary): 
   - 3-second commit window for reconnects when the same request_id is presented; duplicates within the window and with the same request_id will be deduplicated and not billed. 
   - Client retries that do not preserve request_id are subject to billing.
   - For long-lived streams, Redwood recommends using the session-resume header (x-rw-session-id) and issuing a finalization call to reduce billing ambiguity.

3) Minimal engineering checklist (what Novamed needs to do to benefit): 
   - Ensure client retries include the original request_id.
   - Preserve session id header on reconnects.
   - If commit semantics are available, call the commit endpoint when the client has received final output.

Next steps: if you confirm you'd like the pilot credit and the amendment language above, I'll route the ask to Finance and Legal and set up a 30-minute call to walk the invoice lines. Proposed slot: Monday 2026-08-09 10:30 AM PT. Does that work?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best,
